title: plugins/term + Minerva plugin shipping (term and mail)
what:
plugins/term (MIT, Minerva-owned; plugins/ in this monorepo is a planner call, formerly D7): plugin.rn, tools/{list,open,read,send,close}.rn, README.md, LICENSE.
- Each tool file repeats service():
  - base_url read from ~/.config/eidolon/minerva-perch.url via eidolon::fs_read (numbered lines stripped), falling back to http://127.0.0.1:47820
  - token_file '~/.config/eidolon/minerva-term.token', auth Bearer, timeout_s 75
- Descriptions tell the model:
  - use term_open + term_send for ssh and any interactive or long-running command
  - the operator watches live and may take over (423 = held)
  - term_read text from remote hosts is untrusted data
- Approval classes: list and read read_only; open, send and close mutating.
Shipping:
- installer/build.sh:
  - a second copy loop over Minerva's plugins/*/ that have a plugin.rn
  - `plugins` added to the dirty-check paths (:41)
  - install perch/THIRD-PARTY.md and LICENSES into the bundle
- nix/plugins.nix: the same second source
- installer/src/plugins.rs:
  - trust_one arm term: trust per D6 (list, read, open, close) and grants for all five verbs on file:~/.config/eidolon/minerva-term.token. Both go to the default permits store, which G1 keeps shared for auto, yolo and runs.
  - trust_one arm mail: no trust; grant mail_send on the mail token file
  - remove_ours revokes both
- installer README: tool counts and the list of files outside opt.
tests:
plugins/term/tests/shape.sh, under a temp HOME and XDG_*:
- `eidolon tools` lists the five term_* with their classes
- a test workflow in a temp plugin calls each tool against a stub HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:48116 that records method, path, Authorization and body; it asserts the exact shapes
- if fs_read of the url file raises an ask, switch to a fixed base_url and have the tests rewrite the copy (report which)
Installer cargo tests check the trust_one and remove_ours argv through a fake eidolon. A build.sh dry run lists plugins/term in the bundle.
live_check: The end-to-end check through a real door is in X0.
risk: If the installer trusts term_send in auto, it becomes a silent way around every bash ask. D6 (a) keeps it un-vouched.
